examples.title: Read a field before expanding the array
Expand one order into its items
examples.sql:
SELECT id, order_data.customer AS customer,
       unnest(order_data.items).sku AS sku
FROM orders
ORDER BY id, sku;

examples.title: Keep the order with no items
examples.sql:
SELECT o.id, o.order_data.customer AS customer,
       item.sku AS sku, item.qty AS qty
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN UNNEST(o.order_data.items) AS u(item) ON true
ORDER BY o.id, sku;

sampleSpecs.title: Three complete order documents
sampleSpecs.description: Every document is shown. Ben has an empty items array; his order still exists.

challenge.title: Count items, including an empty order
challenge.prompt: Return id and item_count for every order. Count item rows, not units, and keep orders with zero items.
challenge.hint: After a LEFT JOIN, count a non-NULL item field. COUNT(*) also counts the placeholder row for Ben.
challenge.starter:
SELECT o.id, count(*) AS item_count
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN UNNEST(o.order_data.items) AS u(item) ON true
GROUP BY o.id ORDER BY o.id;
challenge.solution:
SELECT o.id, count(item.sku) AS item_count
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN UNNEST(o.order_data.items) AS u(item) ON true
GROUP BY o.id ORDER BY o.id;
challenge.success: Three orders remain, and Ben correctly has zero items.
